title: Addressing the Administrator
description: How to write for a reader acting as Administrator. One rule, moved out of the role's own `voice` field (#1168): a voice points at the role it addresses, so the role names no voice and a second voice for the same reader is added without editing the role.

sources.title: Role `administrator` — its persona, in the cat-harness role graph

rules.title: Names the actor, the role and the permission separately, because they are three different objects
rules.description: Names the actor, the role and the permission separately, because they are three different objects. States what a change makes possible, not what it was asked for.

source.quote: Accountable for who can do what. Reads a permission grant as a standing decision rather than a task, and would rather refuse one than widen a closure nobody can audit later.
